author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: Breaking change: openmoss configs with backend: rocm or rocm_bin no longer resolve. The BackendDescriptor::support list in openmoss.h had the rocm row removed, bin_variants trimmed to ['vulkan', 'cuda'], rocm version pin and asset checksums dropped from backend_versions.json, rocm_bin removed from defaults.json, and the TheRock loader-path branch in openmoss_server.cpp dead-code was removed. The PR acknowledges this and documents the migration.
evidence.documentation: README.md support table, docs/dev/backends-reference.md backend matrix and capabilities table, docs/guide/configuration/README.md config example, and generated regions were all updated. The PR author notes 'Generated regions regenerated from the descriptor; no generated region hand-edited.' All user-facing docs reflect the removal.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This commit removes a user-reachable configuration path: openmoss configs with backend: rocm or rocm_bin overrides no longer resolve. The PR describes a migration (use vulkan or cuda, or backend: auto). The PR is intentionally temporary ('merge this PR asap...revert this PR and apply the fix'). No evidence shows a human exercised the Vulkan-only openmoss path end-to-end on a ROCm-capable system. The residual risk is that a user on AMD hardware with OpenMOSS now has to switch backend and re-download the binary — the Vulkan and CUDA code paths remain untouched, but nobody demonstrated the post-merge configuration resolves cleanly on a real machine.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. There is exactly one commit (a590a205e0ebad53c31dcc2076aac4cc4a37c044) and the approval was cast against that same commit. No churn between approval and merge.
evidence.review: PR approved by @pwilkin (subject-matter expert for OpenMOSS per contribute.md) at 17:26:30Z, about 18 minutes after the PR was opened and 27 minutes before merge. @pwilkin responded 'Wow, this is stupid :O yeah, by all means, let's do the hotfix' confirming he understands the rationale. No inline review comments were posted beyond the approval. The PR is explicitly framed as a stop-gap hotfix with a plan to revert once a real fix lands, which @pwilkin acknowledged.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change removes dead code and unused download assets (ROCM checksums in backend_versions.json). No network calls, credential handling, or supply-chain surface was added or modified beyond removing the ROCm binary pins.
evidence.tests: CI passed across all workflows (C++ build, docker-smoke-test, CodeQL, MCP smoke test, server download registry, etc.). The two OpenMOSS audio-generation CI jobs had their backends trimmed from 'vulkan rocm' to 'vulkan' — appropriate for the change. The test/utils/capabilities.py file was updated to remove rocm from the openmoss backend list. No existing tests were weakened, deleted, or inappropriately skipped.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server with an OpenMOSS config and confirm that selecting backend "vulkan" or "cuda" works correctly, since the ROCm path no longer exists.

subject: Remove OpenMOSS ROCm support on all operating systems (#3615)
summary: Removes ROCm backend support for OpenMOSS (TTS and audio generation) on Windows and Linux because ROCm builds run ~40x slower than Vulkan on the same hardware, and marks the change as a hotfix pending a real fix.
verdict_reason: This is a hotfix merge with clear expert review from @pwilkin (OpenMOSS subject-matter expert per contribute.md), but it is a deliberate breaking change that temporarily removes user-facing ROCm support and explicitly acknowledges a real fix is still pending.
